messages:
anya: quick note: onboarding run for ricochet-13b (int8) hit sporadic OOMs on a couple prod-sim P40s during long-context workflows (user history ~4k tokens). posting short debug thread.
liam: saw it on the dashboard. OOMs cluster around long-history summarization and mult-turn Q&A. batch=4, max_new_tokens was left at 200 for the canary.
sandeep: fwiw our allocator metrics show many small hole fragments after streaming KV writebacks. fragmentation ratio jumped to 0.42 before crash.
anya: raw host trace snippet: ```Kernel memcpy failed: CUDA_OUT_OF_MEMORY
GPU total: 48GB, used highwater: 46.2GB, free: 1.8GB
KV cache estimate: 35.5GB
Slab free segments: 1242 small (<64KB) fragments
Req tokens (history+gen): 4120
Batch size: 4, max_new_tokens: 200```
liam: ok that confirms allocator churn. int8 changed per-layer block alignment so allocations no longer coalesce well. we should test two paths: compacting allocator and reduced per-request token caps.
sandeep: propose immediate canary config changes: - max_new_tokens -> 96 - enable soft_truncate_on_context_overflow true (truncate earliest turns) - runtime flag: enable_small_alloc_pool to aggregate tiny allocations
anya: microbenchmark: small_alloc_pool reduced fragmentation ratio 0.42 -> 0.18 on synthetic long-dialogs. combined with max_new_tokens=96 we avoided OOMs in 5k requests. latency p95 +8% in worst-case.
liam: that perf hit might be ok for hosted, but for Dedicated customers we should offer an opt-in "high-context" profile with fp16. also, can we patch scheduler to stagger large-history requests by adding a jittered start?
sandeep: scheduler jitter saved ~12% simultaneous KV spikes in our sim. implementable as small change in route executor.
anya: about quality: the int8 variant shows a small delta on our long-summary evals: ROUGE-L down ~0.9. not huge but noticeable for some customers. testing int4-hybrid didn't help; fp16 baseline is best.
liam: routing idea: label routes with a signal 'quality_critical' and allow per-route model policy. For now set summarization endpoint to prefer fp16; fallback to int8 only if capacity pressure < threshold.
sandeep: rollout plan suggestion: 1) enable small_alloc_pool and scheduler jitter in canary (eng-staging) 2) lower default max_new_tokens to 96 for ricochet-int8 canary 3) tag /summarize routes as quality_critical -> prefer fp16 4) run 72h soak with mixed prompt corpus 5) monitor metrics: OOM rate, frag_ratio, ROUGE-L drift 6) rollback if ROUGE-L drop >0.5 or OOM rate >0.05%
liam: agreed. i'll add alert rules and a dashboard tile for frag_ratio. canary PR pls include exact flag names and a fallback timeout (e.g., if fp16 fallback increases latency by >200ms for 2m then re-evaluate).
anya: opening PR now with config diffs. will attach eval snapshot and microbench numbers.
ops-bot: canary job queued: ricochet-13b:int8 flags=[max_new_tokens=96,small_alloc_pool=on,scheduler_jitter=25ms]; target=eng-staging; started=2026-03-24T09:12Z
liam: thanks. once soak completes we should document guidance: "ricochet-13b/int8: prefer shorter max_new_tokens or use fp16 for long-context/high-quality routes" and include recommended per-route policy snippets.
sandeep: also adding task to explore an async KV compaction pass that runs during low-load windows. might reduce long-term fragmentation without perf hit.
anya: noted. will track compaction R&D separately. closing this thread unless new hits show up. :white_check_mark:
